title: Sprint 1 — Project Foundation & Database Models
description: Set up the Express application factory and implement relational database models for Users and Tasks.
lab_title: Node.js & Express Todo REST API Lab

tickets.title: Ticket 1 - Initialize Express Application & Health Check
tickets.description:
Initialize the Express application using the application factory pattern (`createApp`). Configure the SQLite database connection and establish a baseline health check endpoint.

### Requirements
1. In `src/app.js`, implement and export `createApp(customConfig)`.
2. Configure SQLite database path pointing to `todo.db` in `src/config.js`.
3. Register a health check route `GET /api/health` that returns JSON `{"status": "healthy"}` with HTTP 200 OK.
4. Ensure the application runs from `src/server.js` on `http://127.0.0.1:5000`.
learning_objectives: Understand the Express application factory pattern.
Learn how to configure database connection settings in Node.js.
Implement and verify basic JSON endpoints and HTTP status codes.
common_mistakes: Returning plain text or HTML instead of JSON.
Hardcoding configuration inside routes instead of using config module.
hints: Use `res.status(200).json({ status: 'healthy' })` to return JSON responses.

tickets.title: Ticket 2 - Design and Implement User Model
tickets.description:
Create the `User` model in `src/models/user.js` for SQLite. Ensure passwords are never stored in plain text by implementing password hashing helpers with `bcryptjs`.

### Model Specifications: `users` Table
- `id`: Integer, primary key, auto-incrementing.
- `username`: String (TEXT), unique, non-nullable.
- `email`: String (TEXT), unique, non-nullable.
- `password_hash`: String (TEXT), non-nullable.
- `created_at`: DateTime (TEXT), defaults to current timestamp.

### Helper Methods
- `hashPassword(password)`: Hashes the plain password using `bcryptjs.hashSync`.
- `comparePassword(password, hash)`: Verifies password against `password_hash` using `bcryptjs.compareSync`.
- `toDict(user)`: Serializes user info excluding `password_hash`.
learning_objectives: Understand relational data modeling with SQLite in Node.js.
Implement secure password hashing using bcrypt.
Prevent accidental exposure of password hashes in serialization.
common_mistakes: Storing plain text passwords in the database.
hints: Set `UNIQUE NOT NULL` constraints on username and email columns.

tickets.title: Ticket 3 - Design Task Model with User Relationship
tickets.description:
Implement the `Task` model in `src/models/task.js` and link it to the `User` model via a foreign key relationship.

### Model Specifications: `tasks` Table
- `id`: Integer, primary key, auto-incrementing.
- `user_id`: Integer, foreign key referencing `users.id`, non-nullable.
- `title`: String (TEXT), non-nullable.
- `description`: Text (TEXT), nullable.
- `is_completed`: Boolean/Integer (0 or 1), default `0`, non-nullable.
- `created_at`: DateTime (TEXT), defaults to current timestamp.
- `updated_at`: DateTime (TEXT), defaults to current timestamp, updates on modification.

### Helper Methods
- `toDict(task)`: Returns an object representation of the task (`id`, `user_id`, `title`, `description`, `is_completed`, `created_at`, `updated_at`).
learning_objectives: Configure foreign key constraints and cascade rules.
Handle timestamp tracking on create and update.

tasks.title: Define `Task` model with foreign key pointing to `users.id`.
Configure relationship and cascade delete between `User` and `Task`.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to set `is_completed` default value to `false` (0).
hints: Use `FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE` in table creation.
